name: Chroma
model: Collections of records: id, embedding, document text and metadata; vector, full-text and metadata-filtered search; Python/JS clients
engine_note: Local and single-node: SQLite plus HNSW index on local disk. Distributed and Chroma Cloud: WAL and SPANN index on object storage, SSD caches
consistency: Per-record operations, no multi-record transactions documented. Distributed: a write is acknowledged after the write-ahead log persists it; queries consult the log so results include acknowledged writes; indexes are rebuilt by a background compactor.
scaling: Three modes, one API: embedded in your process, one server, or distributed (separate gateway, log, query and compactor services on object storage), sold as Chroma Cloud.
reach: Reach for it to prototype RAG in a notebook or app with no server, then move to Chroma Cloud with the same API when it grows.
avoid: Avoid self-hosting the distributed mode yourself (it is built for Chroma Cloud), or when you need transactions with your relational data.
escape: It is a zero-setup local vector store for prototypes; pgvector needs a running Postgres first.
chat: A local prototype store of message embeddings while building retrieval, before production.
notes: Quotes: 'Chroma delegates as much as possible to durable, well-understood subsystems such as SQLite and cloud object storage'; 'You can use Chroma Cloud, which is the managed offering of distributed Chroma.'; distributed doc: 'The log is Chroma's write-ahead log.', 'Records writes before they are acknowledged to clients.', 'After the log persists the write, the gateway acknowledges the request.', query executor 'consults the log to serve a consistent result'; configure doc: 'In Single Node Chroma collections, we use an HNSW ... index' and 'In Distributed Chroma and Chroma Cloud collections, we use a SPANN ... index'. Single-node durability (SQLite settings) not checked. Latest release 1.5.9 (2026-05-05) on both GitHub and PyPI; no newer release in five months. Advice against self-hosting distributed is my inference from the docs framing, not a vendor statement. No Jepsen analysis.
